To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the most significant imaging modalities for the objective prediction and assessment of pancreatic patholologies in association with occurrence of POPF are acoustic radiation force impulse (ARFI) US, CT and/or MRI, and multi-detector row (MD) CT and/or MRI.
acoustic radiation force impulse ultrasonography, contrast-enhanced computed CT/MRI and multi-detector row computed CT/MRI can objectively predict the incidence of POPF after pancreaticoduodenecy.

acoustic radiation force impulse US electrography, contrast-enhanced CT and/or MRI and multi-detector row US, CT, and/or MRI can be used for the objective prediction and risk assessment of POPFs after PD.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing an accurate and objective imaging platform for preoperatively assessing pancreatic pathologies and predicting the risk of POPF after pancreaticoduodenectomies.
the development of an objective and universal preoperative imaging evaluation of POPF after pancreatic resection.
the preoperative evaluation of pancreatic pathologic conditions that are associated with the occurrence of pancreatic fistula in patients undergoing PD.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
preoperative imaging evaluation of the pancreatic pathologies for objective risk assessment of POPFs after PD is a promising and useful strategy for individualized surgical management.
the preoperative assessment of the pancreatic head using these imaging modalities would provide a valuable objective prediction of POPF after pancreatic head resection.

the preoperative evaluation of the pancreas with the use of imaging modalities, which can objectively assess pancreatic pathologies in relation to POPF after PD, should be performed in the near future.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the preoperative imaging assessment for the objective prediction POPF after PD is feasible and would be beneficial for both clinical practice and clinical trials involving PD procedures.
the application of these imaging modalities would be beneficial for the objective prediction and management of POPF after pancreaticoduodenectomies.

the objective assessment of the elastic, fibrotic, and fatty properties of the pancreases is useful for predicting POPF after PD, and that the application of these imaging modalities would be beneficial in the clinical setting of pancreatic head resection.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of these imaging modalities can be helpful for the accurate prediction of POPF occurrence after PD.
these recently developed imaging modalts can be used for the preoperative assessment of the pancreatic pathologies that are associated with the occurrence of pancreatic fistula.

the preoperative risk of POPF after pancreatic head resection can be accurately assessed by the combination of acoustic radiation force impulse US electrography, contrast-enhanced CT/MRI, and multi-detector row computed tomography/MRI.
